label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
To: ashbourne-terrace-chimney
Replying to: p05
Cc: none
Subject: Please do not enter no. 43

Mick, please don’t go into 43 at 9, and please don’t take your lad in either. Priya, please don’t arrange a key for this. I know you’re trying to help, Mick, but putting props under the bay ceiling would mean standing beneath a holed roof with a damaged stack still above it. That’s a very dangerous place to be. The floors may also be carrying fallen debris, and we don’t know how the damaged structure is carrying its weight now. Please don’t inspect the loft from inside either.

I’m a chartered structural engineer with IStructE, but I’m speaking here as a neighbour who looked from the opposite pavement, not as someone carrying out an inspection. This isn’t a commission and I have no professional indemnity cover for free advice.

At about 7 this morning I could see roughly 1.2 metres of the stack at 41 still standing and leaning towards 43, with washed-out mortar at its base. The front roof of 43 is holed, there’s a stepped crack in the brickwork above the bay, and the bay head appears to have dropped. There are also loose slates at the gutter line over the pavement by 43 and 45. This is what I could see from outside; I can’t tell what is happening inside or to the party wall.

Priya, I can’t say whether Mrs Doherty is safe or make that decision for her. I couldn’t see obvious damage to the front of 45, but that doesn’t establish that it’s safe. Personally, I wouldn’t sleep in the front room tonight; I’d rather stay with family until 45 has been checked.

Please use the other side of the road until the council has been, especially on the school run. The tape is across 43’s front garden, not the pavement. The council already knows, but the footway has not been closed. Their dangerous structures out-of-hours service is reached via the main council number, so please report the open pavement and loose slates.

Jo, your cousin isn’t wrong that these terraces are generally robust, but this one is damaged. That’s a different matter.
